issues.legal_issue: A purchaser may terminate a flat-purchase agreement and seek a refund with compensation when the builder unreasonably delays possession, and the purchaser need not accept possession offered after that delay.
material_facts: The builder did not apply for the occupancy certificate or offer possession within the period stipulated in the agreement, including its grace period, and possession was offered more than two years later while the consumer complaint was pending.
The purchaser filed a consumer complaint seeking a refund, said that he did not want the belated possession, and had arranged alternate accommodation.
The purchaser had paid for the flat with the assistance of a loan.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was justified in terminating the agreement by filing the consumer complaint and was entitled to a refund with appropriate compensation; he could not be compelled to accept the belatedly offered possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(o) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, paid construction or building services are consumer services, and an inordinate delay in handing over possession is a deficiency of service. A purchaser need not wait indefinitely and may seek a refund with compensation: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta, (1994) 1 SCC 243, and Fortune Infrastructure v. Trevor D’Lima, (2018) 5 SCC 442. A consumer complaint seeking that relief may constitute termination in the circumstances of this case.

rule.if: consumer_flat_purchase_dispute and builder_missed_possession_deadline and possession_was_unreasonably_delayed and purchaser_rejected_late_possession

predicates.consumer_flat_purchase_dispute: A purchaser brought a consumer proceeding against a builder concerning a flat-purchase agreement.
predicates.builder_missed_possession_deadline: The builder did not obtain the required approval and offer possession within the agreed period, including any grace period.
predicates.possession_was_unreasonably_delayed: The builder offered possession only after a substantial delay beyond the agreed period.
predicates.purchaser_rejected_late_possession: The purchaser declined the belated possession and sought a refund, having arranged alternate accommodation.

issues.definition: When a purchaser in a consumer flat-purchase dispute faces an unreasonably delayed possession offer and rejects it, the purchaser may terminate and receive a refund with compensation.

issues.legal_issue: One-sided and unreasonable terms in a standard-form flat-purchase agreement are not binding on a purchaser who had no meaningful choice but to accept them.
material_facts: The agreement imposed substantially greater payment, cancellation, and forfeiture consequences on the purchaser than consequences on the builder for delayed possession.
The purchaser had to wait beyond the agreed possession period, give notice, and allow further time for a refund, while the builder faced comparatively limited consequences for delay.
The agreement was framed by the builder, and the court found its terms ex facie one-sided, unfair, and unreasonable.
issues.conclusion: The builder could not rely on the one-sided contractual terms to bind the purchaser; incorporating such terms in the circumstances constituted an unfair trade practice.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(r) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 defines unfair trade practices and provides an illustrative, not exhaustive, list. Under Article 14 and Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly, (1986) 3 SCC 156, courts will not enforce an unfair and unreasonable contract or term where there is inequality of bargaining power and the weaker party has no meaningful choice. The court also referred to the Law Commission of India’s 199th Report on unfair contract terms.

rule.if: consumer_flat_purchase_dispute and builder_prepared_standard_form and purchaser_had_no_meaningful_choice and contract_remedies_materially_favored_builder

predicates.consumer_flat_purchase_dispute: A purchaser brought a consumer proceeding concerning a flat-purchase agreement with a builder.
predicates.builder_prepared_standard_form: The builder framed the agreement in a standard form for purchasers to accept.
predicates.purchaser_had_no_meaningful_choice: The purchaser had no meaningful option other than accepting the builder's contractual terms.
predicates.contract_remedies_materially_favored_bui: The agreement imposed substantially harsher consequences on the purchaser than on the builder for comparable breaches or delay.

issues.definition: Where a builder-prepared standard form leaves a purchaser with no meaningful choice and materially favors the builder, its one-sided terms are not binding on the purchaser.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer commission may uphold reasonable interest on a refund for delayed possession by applying the applicable real-estate rule, rather than limiting compensation to the lower rate in an unfair agreement.
material_facts: The builder failed to offer possession within the agreed time, and the purchaser sought a refund.

The consumer commission applied the applicable state rule to determine interest on the refund and did not award interest for the period when an order restraining cancellation, sought by the purchaser, was in operation.
The purchaser had financed the purchase with a bank loan and continued to incur loan interest.
issues.conclusion: The interest award was equitable and lawful, including its exclusion of interest for the period when the purchaser-requested restraint was in operation; the builder's challenge to the rate was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: When possession is not delivered within the specified time, the allottee is entitled to a refund with reasonable interest from the dates of payment until refund: Bangalore Development Authority v. Syndicate Bank, (2007) 6 SCC 711. The court upheld the consumer commission’s application of Rule 15 of the Haryana Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Rules, 2017, which provides for interest at the State Bank of India’s highest marginal cost of lending rate plus two percent. The commission’s exclusion of the period during which the purchaser-requested restraint was in operation supported the equitable nature of the award.

predicates.appeal_from_consumer_refund_award: A builder appealed a consumer commission's order awarding a purchaser a refund for delayed possession.
predicates.builder_failed_to_deliver_possession_on_: The builder did not offer possession within the agreed period or a reasonable time thereafter.
predicates.applicable_real_estate_rule_sets_refund_: A rule applicable to the transaction specifies the rate of interest payable on a refund for failure to deliver possession.
predicates.commission_excluded_purchaser_requested_: The consumer commission did not award interest for a period when a restraint requested by the purchaser was in operation.

issues.definition: When a builder appeals a consumer refund award after failing to deliver possession on time, and the commission applies the applicable refund-interest rule while excluding a purchaser-requested restraint period, the interest award is upheld.
